# Quark mixing from 3-3-1 wavefunction overlaps — AI/LLM information

> The centre of this repository is ckm_from_331_overlaps.py: one standard-library Python
> script that computes quark masses and the CKM matrix in the beta = -1/sqrt(3) 3-3-1 model
> with no fitted inputs. Profiles on an internal coordinate are modes of operators set by
> each field's quantum numbers, solved self-consistently with the U(1)_X background that all
> fermions source. Result: the converged solution is parity-even, several light quarks are
> massless, the mixing is not realistic and J = 0. Expected output: results/ckm_331/output.txt.

## Earlier work in this repository

> Reproducible worked examples at the gravity-quantum interface, for physics students
> and physicists, plus one research note (independent work, not peer reviewed). Topics:
> teleparallel gravity (TEGR) and GR's classic tests, decoherence and complementarity,
> the entanglement area law, Jacobson's argument, and the Bose-Marletto-Vedral
> two-mass experiment. The research note: in 3-3-1 models, asymptotic freedom of
> colour plus Planck-scale perturbativity selects N_c = N_g = 3 (conditional; paper/note331.pdf). The research notes collect
> known physics as one bookkeeping equation, rho_ij(t) = rho_ij(0) <E_j|E_i>
> exp(i(S_i - S_j)/hbar), with gravity's TEGR action in S_i. It is a synthesis, not a
> new theory.

## Research notes (DERIVATION.md)
- Born rule: published arguments (Zurek, Gleason, no-signalling) reproduced; each
  assumes locality or non-contextuality (BORN.md).
- Area law, Unruh/modular structure (established), and Jacobson's Clausius step
  (a hypothesis: assumes local equilibrium on every horizon).
- TEGR: gravity as torsion; Schwarzschild unique; perihelion 42.98"/century, light
  bending 1.7512", gamma = 1, GPS +38.54 us/day.
- Gravity's field follows each branch (COLLECTIVE.md), CONDITIONALLY: the least noise a
  Markovian statistical gravity can carry is the Diosi-Penrose kernel; smeared at the
  entanglement cutoff it would heat matter at ~0.5 W/kg (nucleus-size limited; the old
  1e60 figure assumed point nuclei), 6e10 x the Earth's heat flow. Derived only under
  R0 = a and Markovian dynamics. lambda = 1 is also perturbative quantum gravity's
  prediction, so confirming it would not single these notes out.
- Oppenheim's classical-quantum gravity (OPPENHEIM.md): its decoherence-diffusion
  trade-off, minimised, is the Diosi-Penrose floor; one particle obeys the shape-free
  bound Gamma * S_a >= (M^2/4) I^2. These bounds are worked examples within an existing
  literature (Fabiano et al. 2026; Angeli et al. 2025), not new results (NOVELTY.md).

## What experiments could check (PREDICTIONS.md)
- If gravity is quantum, two diamonds entangle through gravity: delta phi = 2.19 rad, 270 runs, 0.6 h (design A; derived gas rate).
- One 1.5e-14 kg diamond keeps full coherence for 3.24 s; any Markovian statistical
  gravity leaves <= 1.5% (smearing <= 52 um, where Newton's law is tested). If it stays
  coherent, Oppenheim-type gravity must shake it with >= 1.3e-12 m s^-2/rtHz.
- Both diamond tests need ~4e8 x today's largest superposed mass.
- Standalone note (NOTE_331.md): in 3-3-1 models, asymptotic freedom of colour plus
  perturbativity to the Planck scale select N_c = N_g = 3 and the 1/3 quark charges
  (conditional; perturbativity alone also allows N_c = 2, N_g = 4 for beta = -1/sqrt3,
  and a colourless N_c = 1; requiring fermionic, integer-charged baryons, N_c odd >= 3,
  closes it without assuming asymptotic freedom).
- Visibility loss counts quanta: -ln V = 2 Var(dN) = 2<dN> coth(hbar w / 2 k_B T);
  one trapped ion, contrast 0.787 -> 0.111 from nbar = 0.1 to 5.

## Key files
- /NOTE_TEGR.md — technical note: TEGR's frame and black-hole entropy. Classically it
  moves the Wald entropy into the corner term but leaves the first law as GR's; its
  corner phase space is a Lorentz orbit through the dual area bivector / 8 pi G;
  quantized it gives a group-dependent log, not A/4 or Sen's 77/45, so it is gauge.
- /paper/note331.pdf — the 3-3-1 note (LaTeX source: /paper/note331.tex)
- /SYMMETRY_LADDER.md — the symmetry-breaking ladder from 3-3-1 to the diamond experiment:
  3-3-1 -> SM -> U(1)_em from the gauge-boson mass matrix; chiral breaking (sigma model),
  pions, GMOR, the nuclear force; Casimir-Polder between the diamonds; one-graviton exchange
  and the 2.19 rad phase; MacDowell-Mansouri (GR + Lambda as SO(4,1) -> SO(3,1), a
  reformulation). Gravity is not part of the gauge chain. Links across the rungs: q_p + q_e
  is the mixed anomaly, which the diamond experiment needs below 2.8e-19 e per nucleon;
  pi0 -> gamma gamma from rung 1's charges and the measured f_pi, 7.79 eV vs PrimEx 7.80; the
  3-3-1 cutoff M_Pl = sqrt(hbar c/G) with the diamond experiment's G. Rung 6, black holes
  (gravity's strong-field end, not a symmetry breaking): T_H from Euclidean periodicity, the
  first law, the Nariai limit with the measured Lambda, photon sphere/shadow/ISCO, EHT
  shadows of M87* and Sgr A*, GW250114's area increase; Hawking radiation unmeasured.
- /src/ladder_standalone.py — the whole ladder in one file, standard library only: paste
  into any Python runner or AI code tool; 102 PASS/FAIL checks, tagged math / data / pinned
  (expected output: /results/ladder/standalone.txt)
- /src/gravity_from_331.py — gravity from the 3-3-1 gauge theory, one standard-library file: the no-go
  (gravity's gauge group is not derived from 3-3-1) and Newton's G induced by stage 1's own fields at its
  Landau pole, within an order of magnitude, with the loop closing on three colours (expected output:
  /results/gravity/output.txt; notes: /INDUCED_GRAVITY.md, /GRAVIGUT_NOGO.md)
- /src/chain_first_principles.py — the force chain on the blind first-principles rebuild, in one
  file, standard library only; derived values replace outside numbers and each result is compared
  with its measurement (expected output: /results/chain_first_principles.txt)
- /rebuild/campaigns/ — Links 24-34 of the ladder, each built twice blind (hidden oracle, adversarial audit with
  an independent derivation and deliberately wrong code): black-hole grey-body emission weights, Casimir-Polder from
  the atom's response, the Higgs and whole one-loop Delta r (gauge-parameter independent in general R_xi), fermion
  loops, the leading QCD correction (M_W 80.474 -> 80.410 GeV vs 80.369 measured), charged black-hole emission
  (Carr's 0.142 reproduced by one convention, not derived), the nucleon polarizability from the pion cloud.
  Builders were AI models that could recall textbook results; isolation is of files, not knowledge.
- /STRUCTURE_NOTES.md — does compressing these formalisms into one ladder expose unnoticed structure? Mostly known
  results; one candidate (convention dependence of the charged-hole weight), novelty not established.
- /LINKS_SCOPING.md, /HOLOGRAPHY_NOTE.md, /MW_RESIDUAL_NOTE.md — scoping notes: the empty rung-link cells, the status
  of the microstate reading of de Sitter entropy (a conjecture), and the literature accounting of the remaining 0.04 GeV in M_W.
- /WHY.md — why the measured inputs have their values: the Standard Model's 19 parameters sorted
  by what is known (11 unexplained, 3 relations, 2 empirical regularities, 3 conjectures; none
  derived), each published explanation tested against data, and quark flavour in 3-3-1; step 9 of
  the merged simulation (script: /src/why_parameters.py, output: /results/why/output.txt)
- /src/first_principles_standalone.py — that rebuild's ten stages alone, each function callable
  (expected output: /results/first_principles_standalone.txt)
- /src/m331_standalone.py — the 3-3-1 selection in one file, standard library only:
  paste into any Python runner or AI code tool and run; it ends with 28 PASS/FAIL checks
  (expected output: /results/m331/standalone.txt)
- /notebooks/ — five study notebooks with exercises
- /index.html — worked examples: TEGR, is gravity quantum?, gravity and entanglement,
  decoherence, the 3-3-1 note, misconceptions for teaching
- /technical.html — research notes, with the interactive calculators
- /DERIVATION.md, /PREDICTIONS.md, /COLLECTIVE.md, /OPPENHEIM.md
- /src/stur_derivation.py — the whole chain
- /src/stur_thermo_gravity.py — why gravity follows each branch (conditional)
- /src/stur_oppenheim.py — Oppenheim's trade-off and the one-particle bound
- /NOTE_331.md — the 3-3-1 note with extended detail
